[[Category:Logan Valley Cemetery, Bellwood, Pennsylvania]]
== Biography ==
James was born in 1793.  He passed away in 1875.
== Research Notes ==
=== Original Huntingdon will reviewed — 24 October 2026 ===

The original will names James as a son, joint devisee of the Antis home tract and executor with Taylor. James Glasgow-2577 is the strongest checked adult match: reported born in Blair County on 4 October 1793, with a daughter Mary Ellen reported born there in 1829 and eventual Logan Valley Cemetery burial. His age about31 at probate fits. These profile and daughter details are derivative and their memorial originals were not inspected. The bounded public-catalogue comparison found no closer local same-generation James. The Missouri James-45 remains a compatible alternative by name, generation and broad Pennsylvania origin, but his probable Downington birth and later Missouri household are a weaker locality match. The will supplies no age, wife or residence for its James; select2577 as an80% probable working father connection, retaining the alternative and all vital fields. The original will names wife Margaret, sons Richard, William, John, Samuel, Matthew, James and Taylor, and daughters Hannah and Jane. James and Taylor receive the 322-acre, 72-perch home tract jointly, subject to Margaret’s support and the legacies, and are appointed executors. The register records probate and the grant to both executors on 12 March 1825. The will names no mother for the children, no Hunter maiden surname, and no Scottish father for its testator. The widow Margaret is not automatically each child’s mother. The exact percentage assesses the complete father–child identification and is subjective. The original establishes the named family roles; identification of later adults, precise vital dates, maternal parentage and earlier Scottish ancestry require their own evidence. No live WikiTree save or vital-field change is made.<ref>[https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-L99B-T8NH?cc=1999196&wc=9PM6-7MN%3A268496101%2C268530601 Huntingdon County, Pennsylvania, Wills 1822–1847, volumes 3–4, register pp. 139–140; John Glasgow of Antis Township, will 21 January 1825, proved 12 March 1825; FamilySearch, Pennsylvania Probate Records, image 103 of 607. Original full page and both page details inspected 24 October 2026.]</ref>
